newsitem.title: USA: American Airlines pilots to strike-union official.
newsitem.headline: American Airlines pilots to strike-union official.

text.p: Pilots of American Airlines struck the nation's second-largest carrier at 12:01 a.m. EST on Saturday (0501 GMT), union officials said.
"We're going on strike," Airline Pilots Association spokesman Wally Pitts told reporters. APA President James Sovich ordered pilots to shut down operations nationwide.
"At this time we have been unable to reach a satisfactory agreement," Sovich told APA members in a teleconference.
"Our decision to cease operations is a painful one," he said. He described talks as "tedious and frustrating."
Al Comeaux, spokesman for American Airlines, told reporters: "It's after midnight and we did not reach an agreement. The union has rejected the mediators' final hypothetical solution."

White House spokesman Mike McCurry said President Bill Clinton had signed a decision intervening in the American Airlines strike. Fort Worth-Dallas based American Airlines has 2,200 flights that carry about 200,000 passengers a day.
